title: Leveraging the Spatial Hierarchy: Coarse-to-fine Trajectory Generation via Cascaded Hybrid Diffusion

problem.claim: Fine-grained human mobility trajectories are difficult to make publicly available at large scale because of privacy concerns and substantial data collection costs.

gap.claim: Existing trajectory-synthesis methods often neglect road-network structural constraints or depend on instance-level external supervision, limiting scalable generation of fine-grained, high-fidelity trajectories.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Cardiff, a coarse-to-fine cascaded hybrid diffusion framework for fine-grained, structure-plausible trajectory generation.
Cardiff decomposes generation into discrete road-segment-level latent diffusion and continuous fine-grained GPS-level conditional denoising with noise augmentation.
The framework uses the first-stage segment generation as conditions for constrained GPS-level generation that incorporates road geometry and topology.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three large real-world trajectory datasets reportedly show that Cardiff outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across various metrics.
The authors report that the cascaded progressive generation produces high-fidelity trajectories while adhering to road geometry and topology constraints.
The implementation is reported to be publicly available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Urban mobility data is relevant to economic growth and smart-city applications.
Privacy concerns and collection costs restrict public availability of fine-grained trajectories.
Trajectory synthesis can preserve aggregate spatiotemporal distributions, but prior work may neglect road structure or require instance-level supervision.
Cardiff performs cascaded generation from latent discrete road segments to conditioned fine-grained GPS trajectories.
The authors report structural plausibility, high fidelity, and superior benchmark metrics on three real-world datasets.
